lc_person: Francisco de Vitoria, philosopher and legal scholar; author of Relectiones and De legibus, died 1546.
item_person: Francisco de Vitoria, philosopher and legal scholar associated with the University of Salamanca, died 1546.

evidence.says: Heading uses 1486?-1546, but source notes for El internacionalismo de Vitoria (2005) and El poder de la Iglesia (2018) give birth year 1483. Cites Relectiones morales and De legibus; VIAF 265993805 and GND 118768735.

Item identifies Francisco de Vitoria as philosopher, jurist and University of Salamanca teacher, died 1546. Its 1480 birth statement cites GND 11768239X; the item also contains LC-linked GND 118768735 and VIAF 265993805.
María Martín Gómez, Francisco de Vitoria, Universidad de León literary dictionary (2020), gives 1483-1546 and discusses the earlier disagreements about his birth year.

notes: 1483 is supported by the scholarly university biography and two LC source notes. Birth dating remains historically disputed; neither the uncertain LC heading nor the Wikidata 1480 statement establishes a different person.

lc_person: Gérard Walter, historian and editor; author of Histoire du communisme and work on Robespierre.
item_person: Gérard Walter, historian, biographer and publisher, died 1974.

evidence.says: LC heading gives 1896-1974 and cites Histoire du communisme (1931) and Maximilien de Robespierre (1989); VIAF 100184549, ISNI 0000000110316904.

Item has historian, biographer and publisher occupations; birth statement gives 1890, death 1974. VIAF 100184549 and ISNI 0000000110316904 match LC, though the English description still says 1896-1974.

BnF heading is Walter, Gérard (1890-1974), identifying a historian, scholar and editorial writer. Birth year is 1890; sources include the Paris civil death record. ISNI 0000000110316904 matches LC and Wikidata.

notes: BnF supports 1890 over LC’s 1896. Shared identifiers establish the match; the dissertation citation gives the same name.

lc_person: Dominick Stuart Graham, military historian and emeritus professor at the University of New Brunswick; author of Cassino.
item_person: Dominick Stuart “Toby” Graham, military historian and University of New Brunswick professor, 1920-2013.

evidence.says: LC identifies Dominick Stuart Graham, born 1920, died 2013, citing a Telegraph obituary. It cites Cassino (1971) and Against odds (1998), naming an emeritus professor at the University of New Brunswick.
Article explicitly names Dominick Stuart “Toby” Graham (1920-2013), a military historian at the University of New Brunswick; bibliography includes Cassino. Its Wikidata item link targets Q7811799.

notes: Toby is a nickname for Dominick Stuart. Direct Wikidata retrieval failed; the article’s explicit Q7811799 link, matching full name, dates, institution and book corroborate the supplied item label. The dissertation’s Dominick S. matches LC’s full name.

English label says Louis Trenart, but item identifies a historian at Lille III, born 1914, died 1994; birth name includes Trenard. LC n83036155, VIAF 190023042 and ISNI 0000000398079767 match.

lc_person: Sara S. Berry, historian and economist of African agrarian change, Johns Hopkins University.
item_person: Sara Berry, scholar of African political economies and history at Johns Hopkins University.

evidence.says: LC lists variant Sara S. Berry and cites Cocoa, custom, and socio-economic change in rural Western Nigeria (1975). Its note from American women historians (1996), pages 21-22, explicitly gives birth year 1940 and history/economics appointments including Johns Hopkins.
Article names Sara Sweezy Berry, born 1940, scholar of African political economies at Johns Hopkins. It lists the same 1975 Cocoa book; its Wikidata item link targets Q24898366.
Johns Hopkins History department identifies Sara Berry as professor emerita with a University of Michigan PhD.

notes: LC’s biographical source supports 1940 rather than the supplied Wikidata 1950. Direct item retrieval failed; the article’s explicit Q24898366 link and matching field, institution and book corroborate identity. Sara S. is an LC variant matching the dissertation citation.
